global_organization_chain: Summary chain: ranking task -> four indicators -> fuzzy-consistent weights -> grey degrees -> time correction -> gender -> alternate-weight and rho checks.
Introduction chain: public evaluation need -> qualitative-method limitation -> data opportunity -> four-factor quantitative workflow.
Model chain: weight prerequisite -> fuzzy matrix route -> ideal-reference grey comparison -> descending rank.
Weight chain: ordinal preference -> row totals -> fuzzy-consistent matrix -> column normalization -> geometric mean -> final weights.
Grey chain: candidate matrix -> ideal coach -> normalization -> coefficient -> weighted degree -> rank.
Data chain: eligibility -> candidate list -> NCAA source -> four typed values -> calculation table.
Transfer chain: shared four-field interface -> sport-specific championship and award mapping -> new top-five list.
Comparison chain: model list -> named media lists -> overlap -> limited plausibility conclusion.
Time chain: historical concern -> five era groups -> mean plots -> ANOVA -> correction decision.
Correction chain: era baseline -> factor -> transformed winning rate -> grey rerun -> adjusted rank.
Gender chain: same four fields -> women roster -> rank -> broad claim requiring a scope boundary.
Entropy chain: positive matrix -> normalization -> shares -> entropy -> weights -> alternate rank comparison.
Stability chain: changed preference matrix -> revised weights -> rerun -> top-ten comparison.
Sensitivity chain: fixed roster and weights -> rho sweep -> score tables -> claimed top-ten invariance.
Article chain: reader question -> quantitative method -> three sport lists -> portability claim.
The final warning pass records matrix, test, table, claim, and code defects without replacing positive learning.

main_argument_chains.claim: A coach-ranking task becomes auditable when eligibility, four indicators, weight construction, and ideal-reference aggregation are explicit.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Use the rank only with the same sport, roster, indicator, source, and weight contract.

main_argument_chains.claim: Historical and subgroup extensions require their own evidence rather than inheriting validity from the base rank.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Treat the time and gender claims as conditional scenarios until the test semantics and subgroup design are repaired.

main_argument_chains.claim: Alternate weights and rho values are useful local checks but cannot validate a shared roster and indicator design.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Report set and order sensitivity with integrity checks and seek independent validation separately.

main_argument_chains.claim: A public-facing list is strongest when it traces to typed computations and preserves conflicts and reproducibility limits.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Publish the list with provenance, model, uncertainty, and correction disclosures.

warnings.warning: The prose maps the displayed weight-vector positions to indicators in an order inconsistent with the matrix rows; recompute and relabel before reuse.
